exercise.name: Lever Preacher Curl (Turned Torso)

reference.title: Lever Preacher Curl (Turned Torso)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Lever preacher curl machine (sloped arm pad, lever with handle aligned with the elbow)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Load is user-chosen: curl without lifting the elbow off the pad.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower lowering

cues.text: Sit turned toward the left so the right upper arm lies straight down the sloped pad, armpit over the top edge, elbow lined up with the lever axis; palm up on the handle, left hand on the left thigh.
Breathe out and curl the handle up toward the right shoulder, elbow staying on the pad.
Squeeze the biceps at the top; keep the trunk turned and still.
Breathe in and lower under control along the arc.
Stop with the arm nearly straight; switch sides after the set.

mistakes.fix: Keep the back of the arm on the pad; lighten the load.
Hold the turned trunk still; only the forearm moves.
Line the elbow up with the pivot.
Lower slowly and stop just short of straight.

kinematics.norm: From nearly straight to fully bent, the forearm stopping short of vertical (clinical opinion)
Upper arm resting on the sloped pad; the elbow stays on the lever axis (clinical opinion)
Supinated: palms up on the handle (clinical opinion)
The handle rides an arc about the elbow: the lever pivot is lined up with the elbow joint (clinical opinion)
Turning the trunk lets the working arm lie straight down the pad, the classic preacher position that trains the biceps at long lengths (Kassiano 2025)
About 1.3 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #18438, Lever Preacher Curl (Turned Torso), video (movement reference)
Kassiano et al. 2025, distinct muscle growth and strength adaptations after preacher and incline biceps curls (Int J Sports Med, randomized trial in 63 young women)
Young, Porcari, Camic, Kovacs and Foster 2014, ACE-sponsored EMG study of eight biceps exercises, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse (ACE ProSource, August 2014)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Load is user-chosen: start light; the bottom of a preacher curl stretches the biceps and elbow.
Do not let the handle drop into the straight-arm position.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Elbow discomfort at the bottom: stop just short of straight.
progressions: Pause for 2 s at the bottom of the range.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Prime mover: bends the elbow and turns the palm up.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handles and help bend the elbow (brachioradialis).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm on the pad.
